text: There was a hare with very fast feet, and a tortoise with a hard shell (literally: "hard on the outside"), who was very slow. The hare laughed: "You're so slow!" The tortoise said: "Let's race, and see who gets to that big tree first!" They set off. The hare was soon far ahead. He looked back: the tortoise was far behind. He said: "I'll take a little nap, it doesn't matter." He lay down by the road and fell asleep. The tortoise was very slow, but she didn't stop and didn't sleep; she kept going, little by little. She reached the sleeping hare, and then passed him. The hare woke up and looked: the tortoise was almost at the big tree! He ran with all his strength, but the tortoise got there ahead of him. Being slow doesn't matter. If you don't stop, you will get there.

blind.whole: A fable about a race. A small animal with long ears (a rabbit or hare), called Kuài-kuai, has fast feet and laughs at a slow animal with a hard outer body (a tortoise or turtle), called Yìng-ying. Yìng-ying suggests a race to a big plant, probably a tree. Kuài-kuai gets far ahead, decides a short sleep won't matter, and lies down by the road. Yìng-ying is slow but doesn't stop or sleep, so he walks past the sleeping Kuài-kuai. Kuài-kuai wakes up, sees Yìng-ying is nearly there, and runs as hard as he can, but Yìng-ying arrives first. The lesson: being slow doesn't matter; if you don't stop, you will get there.
blind.unsure: Sentence 5: 'the outside of its body is very hard' together with walking slowly reads best as a tortoise or turtle, but it could also be a snail or another shelled animal. Sentence 9 and later: 'dà zhíwù' (big plant) is most likely a big tree, but the text only says big plant. Sentences 16 and 26: 'děng' is glossed 'to wait'. I read 'méi děng' / 'bù děng' as not stopping or pausing along the way. A literal reading, 'he did not wait (for anyone)' / 'if you don't wait', is possible but makes less sense. Sentence 22: the gloss splits 'kuài-yào' into 'fast' + 'to want', but taken together with the closing 'le' I read it as 'is about to (arrive)'. A literal reading, 'quickly wants to arrive', is less likely. Sentence 23: 'kuài zǒu' is literally 'walk fast'. I read it as running or hurrying.

notes: Translated by hand following the translate skill and the brief (2026-10-22), level the whole dictionary. kb_memory returned the book's own Hao-shuo-de of this story (lesson none, the appendix), so ten sentences adapt it and say so in their source (W19); I did not open src/content or review/translations. Names: the hare and the tortoise have no words (7- and 16-word forms), so each is described once and then given a quoted name (W16, extended to animal characters by the brief): "Kuài-kuai" and "Yìng-ying". The book instead repeats the descriptions jiǎo kuài-de dòng-wù and wài-miàn-yìng-de dòng-wù; tried that first, and every sentence with wài-miàn yìng-de dòng-wù came out at over 500 readings (13 to 18 words), while zhè-ge dòng-wù would not tell the two animals apart. A blind reader may report the names as added; they stand for "the hare" and "the tortoise". Tried and dropped: "Yìng-ying" zài hěn yuǎn-de hòu-miàn (and the book's version with the description) reads only as a noun phrase, the far back where Ying-ying is, in all 63 readings, so far behind is zài hòu-miàn, hěn yuǎn; "bǐ tā zǎo dào le" reads only with bǐ tā zǎo as a subject (8 readings), so ahead of him is dào-de bǐ tā zǎo; yǐ-jīng is not a word (already is le); yī-diǎn yī-diǎn before a verb reads as clock times, the book's own Wǒ-de jiā yī-diǎn yī-diǎn biàn hǎo. reads first as clock times too. The race sentence's meant reading is perceive-doing plus a serial verb (we see who is fastest, reaching that big tree): no reading puts zuì kuài on dào. Three sentences are over 10 words (9: 13 words, 11 and 22: 11 words); all are one idea, so they were not split. dà zhíwù (big plant) stands for big tree, as in the book's sentence; the dictionary's tree is dà-de zhíwù. Tool notes: the brief's example kb_lookup '{"query":...}' fails, the argument is word; each CLI process took about 2 to 5 minutes to load in this session, so calls were batched in one node process with openKb and callTool. Glossary proposal: stop (pause on the way) -> méi děng / bù děng: the dictionary's form of 一口气 (without stopping) is zhōng-jiān bù děng, and bù dòng (the form of 停) says standing still. Glossary proposal: far behind -> zài hòu-miàn, hěn yuǎn: X zài hěn yuǎn-de hòu-miàn reads only as a noun phrase. Glossary proposal: got there before him -> dào-de bǐ tā zǎo: bǐ tā zǎo dào le reads only with bǐ tā zǎo as a subject. Glossary proposal: kept going -> hái zài zǒu: still walking; zǒu-xià-qù gives 473 readings and verb-xià-qù reads also as going down. Glossary proposal: it doesn't matter -> méi guānxi: the mei-guanxi pattern, shorter than the book's méi-yǒu guānxi. Glossary proposal: almost at -> kuài-yào dào ... le: kuai-quick's about to; plain kuài dào can read as arriving quickly.
